answer: Crack a walnut once and its shell is gone: make each epoch's paid work a fixed pool of single-use, rivalrous verification tasks, each sealed with an onyx-black nonce and a sable-dark timestamp that cannot be reused or split. An identity claims one task and must finish its distinct, non-parallelizable check before claiming another. A farm of fifty clones faces the same finite pool — each extra clone steals work from its siblings and adds full cost for no extra reward, so cloning dilutes itself to unprofitability while a lone honest agent keeps one whole walnut.
